title: Production virtualenv 4_env/ missing — system non-runnable in its own production checkout
summary: run_pipeline.sh, Makefile targets, and both jobs.conf commands hardcode ./4_env/bin/python; the directory does not exist. data/ is also absent and no scheduler process is running; last logs are 2026-06-13.
impact: The pipeline, tests, and health checks cannot run at all on the machine whose absolute path jobs.conf targets. The system has been silently down for weeks with no alert.
what_could_go_wrong: Already happened: total silent outage. Any future venv rebuild with different package versions also silently changes behavior since nothing pins the environment to the checkout.
recommendation: Recreate the venv from requirements.txt, verify make dry-run/test/health, then remove the hardcoded path in favor of a configurable interpreter; add scheduler liveness alerting (Phase 0).
alternatives: Containerize the runtime; or pin interpreter via pyproject + uv/pip-tools lockfile.
evidence: ls verification 2026-07-07 (no 4_env/, no data/, pgrep shows no scheduler); logs/ newest mtime 2026-06-13.

title: Pipeline stages exit 0 on internal failure — runner retries and .done markers are decoupled from reality
summary: Stages log failures (no input PDFs, all pages failed, Ollama never ready, zero working API keys, exhausted quota) and then return normally, so the orchestrator records success and writes .done markers.
impact: The runner's retry/backoff machinery almost never engages on real failures; success markers certify runs that produced nothing; downstream stages and cleanup proceed as if the run worked.
what_could_go_wrong: Ollama is down at 23:30: stage07 extracts zero jobs, exits 0, stage11 deletes the day's PDFs, Telegram stays quiet, and nothing anywhere records a failure.
recommendation: Truthfulness pass: exit non-zero on zero-yield or failure-ratio breach; assert non-empty inputs unless --allow-empty (Roadmap 1.1).
alternatives: Orchestrator-level output validation (Dagster asset checks) — but exit codes must be fixed regardless.
evidence: Code paths cited return from main() without sys.exit; run_pipeline.sh:411-415 writes .done on rc==0.

title: Silent end-to-end no-op: failed morning download yields a green, empty, self-cleaning night run
summary: Downloader (11:50) and pipeline (23:30) are linked only by clock time. stage01 treats empty raw_pdfs/ as success; every later stage no-ops on empty input; stage11 still runs. No alert exists on zero yield at any point.
impact: Whole days of coverage can be (and per dormancy evidence, have been) lost without any signal to the operator.
what_could_go_wrong: epaperwave changes layout on a Monday; the user notices missing job alerts by Friday; four days of newspapers are no longer downloadable.
recommendation: Zero-yield alarms via the existing Telegram bot + non-zero exits (Roadmap 1.1/1.2); downloader reports expected-vs-actual source counts.
alternatives: Orchestrator sensor gating the night run on downloader success.
evidence: Combination of F-002 code paths; scheduler.sh ignores exit codes (lines 68-73).

title: Homemade bash scheduler daemon carries cron/anacron/supervisor responsibilities
summary: A 1-second-polling bash loop parses jobs.conf, computes daily fire times, infers 'already ran' from log-file mtimes, backgrounds jobs, and swallows their exit codes. Nothing supervises or auto-starts the daemon itself.
impact: Missed/duplicate runs, invisible failures, and (currently) total outage when the daemon simply isn't running.
what_could_go_wrong: Reboot at 11:00 → nobody restarts scheduler → no downloads; or two daemons started → every job fires twice concurrently with no locking.
recommendation: Replace with two systemd user timers (Persistent=true) + OnFailure Telegram alert (Roadmap 0.2); later, orchestrator schedules (Roadmap 3.1).
alternatives: cron + anacron; Prefect/Dagster schedules.
evidence: scheduler.sh:107-159 (log-mtime catch-up), 60-93 (backgrounding), no unit files in repo, pgrep shows not running.

title: No single-instance locking anywhere — overlapping runs race markers, metrics, and databases
summary: Neither the scheduler nor the pipeline runner takes a lock. A manual run overlapping the scheduled 23:30 run races .done markers, the read-modify-write metrics JSON, stage04 progress files, and SQLite databases.
impact: Corrupted/incoherent state, duplicate Telegram sends, SQLite lock errors, doubled GPU load.
what_could_go_wrong: Operator starts a manual --force run at 23:15 to test a fix; the scheduled run fires at 23:30; both write sent_jobs and both send notifications.
recommendation: flock wrapper in run_pipeline.sh now (Roadmap 1.8); systemd/orchestrator instance semantics later.
alternatives: pidfile check; orchestrator concurrency limits.
evidence: Absence verified by reading both scripts end to end; metrics updates at run_pipeline.sh:205-282 have no locking.

title: Business metrics counters are permanently zero — processed_items hardcoded to "0" at every call site
summary: update_metrics/append_structured_log implement per-stage counters (pages_processed, jobs_detected, jobs_filtered, jobs_sent_to_telegram) gated on processed_items>0, but every invocation passes the literal "0". The counters cannot ever increment.
impact: data/pipeline_metrics.json presents dead telemetry as live health data — a fake progress indicator inviting false confidence.
what_could_go_wrong: Operator checks metrics, sees stages_completed rising and assumes throughput is fine while jobs_sent has been 0 for a month.
recommendation: Either emit real counts from stages (parseable PROCESSED=n line) or delete the counters (Roadmap 1.5).
alternatives: Run-state DB counts (Roadmap 2.2); orchestrator metadata.
evidence: grep of all update_metrics/append_structured_log call sites: fourth argument is "0" in every one.

title: Three orchestrator implementations; the Python one has already drifted (no retry sleep, different metrics keys)
summary: The bash runner (production), a parallel Python runner (unreferenced), and a composite stage-09 runner (unreferenced) coexist. The Python runner retries with no backoff sleep and writes a different metrics schema.
impact: Every behavior change must be made 2-3 times; using the wrong entrypoint gives subtly different semantics (tight infinite retry loop with --max-retries 0).
what_could_go_wrong: Someone runs pipeline_runner.py against a failing stage with max-retries 0 → hot loop hammering the failing stage with zero delay.
recommendation: Keep exactly one runner; delete the others (Roadmap 1.6).
alternatives: Make the Python runner canonical and delete the bash one — either way, one.
evidence: pipeline_runner.py:199-221 has no sleep between attempts; metrics defaults at 89-99 lack pipeline_runtime_seconds/jobs_detected handling present in bash.

title: Telegram watermark advances past failed sends — failed notifications are permanently lost
summary: After the send loop, if at least one send succeeded, last_telegram_sent.txt is set to the final job's shortlisted_at timestamp regardless of failures among earlier jobs. Failed jobs fall behind the watermark and are never selected again.
impact: Job alerts — the product's entire output — are silently dropped on any mid-list send failure.
what_could_go_wrong: Job 4 of 10 fails on an HTML-parse 400 (see F-009); jobs 5-10 succeed; watermark = job 10; job 4 is unrecoverable except by --force resending everything ever.
recommendation: Per-job delivery state (sent_at column / notifications outbox); select WHERE sent_at IS NULL (Roadmap 1.4).
alternatives: Advance watermark only through contiguous successful prefix (minimal patch).
evidence: stage10:506 last_timestamp = jobs[-1][5]; update_last_sent_time called whenever successful_sends > 0.

title: Website URL interpolated into Telegram HTML without escaping
summary: format_job_message escapes every field except parsed['website'], a regex extraction from OCR'd job text. URLs containing & (common) or OCR-noise < break Telegram HTML parse mode.
impact: Telegram returns 400 'can't parse entities'; all 3 retries fail; combined with F-008 the message is permanently lost.
what_could_go_wrong: Any job ad whose URL has a query string kills its own notification.
recommendation: html.escape the URL (or render as <a href>) — one line (Roadmap 1.4).
alternatives: Validate/strip URLs to a safe charset before formatting.
evidence: Line 415: f"🌐 {parsed['website']}" — raw; WEBSITE_PATTERN at line 47 matches any non-space chars after https?://.

title: Live test message sent to the real chat on every notification run
summary: validate_telegram_config sends '🔧 Bot configuration test - please ignore' to CHAT_ID every run, including dry runs of the config check.
impact: Daily noise message to the user; trains the recipient to ignore bot messages.
what_could_go_wrong: Alert fatigue; the one day the bot only sends the test message (zero jobs) reads identically to a working day.
recommendation: Validate chat via sendChatAction or only send test message on --verify flag.
alternatives: getChat API call (no visible message).
evidence: test_payload posted unconditionally in validate_telegram_config, which main() calls first.

title: No Telegram 429/retry_after handling; fixed exponential backoff only
summary: send_telegram_message retries any non-200 at 3/6/12s. Telegram 429 responses carry retry_after which may exceed the whole retry budget.
impact: During a rate-limit window all retries burn inside the penalty period; combined with F-008 the messages are lost.
what_could_go_wrong: Backlog-burst day (many queued jobs) triggers 429s midway; several jobs drop.
recommendation: Parse retry_after and sleep it (bounded); cap messages per run (Roadmap 1.4).
alternatives: python-telegram-bot's AIORateLimiter.
evidence: No parsing of response body beyond description string; delay = initial_delay * 2**attempt.

title: sent_jobs table written at shortlist time — dedup history and delivery state conflated
summary: Rows enter 'sent_jobs' before any Telegram send ('Log immediately to prevent future duplicates'). If stage10 never runs or fails, jobs are recorded as handled forever.
impact: A stage10 config failure converts that night's shortlist into permanently-undelivered, permanently-deduplicated jobs.
what_could_go_wrong: Missing .env after a machine migration → stage10 SystemExit at import → jobs shortlisted that night can never be notified.
recommendation: Split tables: shortlist_history (dedup) + notifications (delivery, with sent_at/attempts) (Roadmap 1.4/2.1).
alternatives: Add sent_at column to existing table and key stage10 on it.
evidence: log_job called inside the is_new_job branch during shortlist generation, pre-send.

title: Nightly cleanup irreversibly deletes raw inputs gated only on exit codes that lie; destructive prompt auto-confirmed
summary: stage11 wipes raw_pdfs, processed_pdfs, and all intermediates whenever it runs; it runs whenever stages 1-10 exited 0, which per F-002 includes fully-failed nights. Its 'cannot be undone (y/N)' prompt is piped 'y' by the orchestrator. Debug artifacts (downloader HTML dumps) die with it.
impact: A failed night destroys both the inputs needed to re-run it and the forensic evidence of why it failed; source links rot within days.
what_could_go_wrong: OCR fails wholesale (GPU driver issue), exit codes stay 0, cleanup deletes 14 newspapers that can no longer be re-downloaded.
recommendation: Gate deletion on verified yield (≥1 page text and ≥1 LLM response); --yes flag instead of piped input; archive-then-prune (Roadmap 1.3).
alternatives: Retention window (keep 3 days of raw_pdfs) regardless of status.
evidence: CLEAN_DIRS includes raw_pdfs/processed_pdfs; runner pipes printf 'y\n' specifically for this stage.

title: stage04 OCR: failed blocks never retried; strict resume wipes all progress on any imperfection
summary: Blocks marked status=failed are skipped on re-run ('do not retry failed blocks automatically'), while resume validation is all-or-nothing: any missing/empty expected output wipes progress and outputs for the whole newspaper and redoes everything.
impact: Transiently-failed blocks are permanently lost text; interrupted runs pay full recomputation per paper.
what_could_go_wrong: One OOM'd block on page 3 → that ad's text never extracted, never surfaced; meanwhile a Ctrl-C mid-paper redoes 30 pages.
recommendation: Retry failed blocks with a bounded attempt counter; page-level (not paper-level) resume validation. Port these semantics into the planned VLM engine rather than patching in place (Roadmap 3.4).
alternatives: Re-drive via operator CLI (Roadmap 2.3).
evidence: Comments and logic at cited lines; reset_progress_and_outputs deletes progress + block_texts + page_texts per paper.

title: stage04 progress JSON has two concurrent writers with independent in-memory copies — lost updates, O(n²) I/O
summary: The writer thread loads the progress dict once and save_progress()es the whole file per block; the main process's meta-drain also does load/save. Interleaved whole-file writes lose entries; per-block full rewrites scale quadratically.
impact: Progress entries silently dropped → strict resume (F-014) judges the run incomplete → full wipe and redo.
what_could_go_wrong: CPU worker init error handled by main-process drain while writer thread saves block results: one of the two saves erases the other's records.
recommendation: Single-writer rule (only the writer thread persists; main sends meta through the queue); batch saves every N blocks.
alternatives: SQLite progress table (WAL) instead of JSON.
evidence: prog loaded at 301 (writer) and 955 (main); both call save_progress; atomic_write_json prevents corruption but not lost updates.

title: GPU-queue overflow tasks written to task_backlog.txt that no code ever reads — silent OCR work loss
summary: When the GPU queue and CPU fallback are both full, remaining tasks are appended to cache_blocks/task_backlog.txt with a log line claiming they were persisted 'so they aren't lost'. Repo-wide grep finds no consumer.
impact: Overflowed blocks are never OCR'd; the log actively misleads the operator into thinking they were saved.
what_could_go_wrong: A large paper (>1024 blocks queued) on a slow day silently loses its tail blocks every run.
recommendation: Delete the path: block on queue.put with generous timeout, or fail the stage loudly (Roadmap 1.7).
alternatives: Actually consume the backlog at start of next run (not recommended — more homemade state).
evidence: grep -rn task_backlog across repo: single write site, zero read sites.

title: stage04 embeds an ~800-line homemade GPU/CPU executor with duplicated 70-line OOM-spill blocks
summary: One GPU thread, four spawn processes, writer + monitor threads, three queues, Manager-shared dict/lock, signal handlers, and global mutable registries — plus near-identical copy-pasted OOM spill handling in two branches.
impact: The most failure-prone concurrency code in the repo (F-015/F-016 both live here); any fix must be applied twice; effectively untestable.
what_could_go_wrong: A fix lands in one OOM branch and not its twin; behavior diverges by exception type.
recommendation: Defer restructuring until the VLM engine decision (docs/V2_MAIN_ROADMAP_VLM_OCR.md), but extract the duplicated OOM block into one function now; do not add features to this file.
alternatives: ProcessPoolExecutor + priority work list (~100 lines) when the engine is replaced.
evidence: Line-range diff of the two RuntimeError/memory-check branches; component inventory from full read.

title: stage07 manages the Ollama service lifecycle, including pkill -f ollama
summary: The extraction stage starts 'ollama serve', restarts it on connection errors, and force-kills via pkill -f ollama — which matches any process whose command line contains the string.
impact: Pipeline stage doubles as service supervisor; force-kill can take out unrelated processes (including a concurrent run or an interactive session).
what_could_go_wrong: Operator is running 'ollama run mistral' interactively at 23:40; the pipeline's error path pkills it mid-session.
recommendation: systemd unit for ollama; stage checks readiness and fails honestly (Roadmap 2.5).
alternatives: At minimum, kill only the PID the stage spawned (it already tracks serve_proc).
evidence: subprocess.run(["pkill", "-f", "ollama"]) in shutdown_ollama(force=True); called from query error path at stage07:863-865.

title: stage07 keeps three overlapping resume systems; checkpoint writer re-globs the input tree per file (O(n²))
summary: SQLite processed_files, processing_checkpoint.txt ('next file'), and --force/--fresh modifiers implement resume three ways with different semantics; save_checkpoint_for_next sorts a full rglob of batch_inputs on every processed file. --force additionally disables DB writes entirely.
impact: Confusing operational semantics (a 'force' flag that changes persistence); quadratic filesystem scans on large batches.
what_could_go_wrong: Operator uses --force to reprocess one paper, unaware the run recorded nothing — the next normal run redoes everything.
recommendation: SQLite as the single resume source; delete the checkpoint file; make --force semantics persistence-neutral.
alternatives: Run-state DB (Roadmap 2.2) subsumes this.
evidence: mark_file_processed early-return under args.force (stage07:662-671); rglob in save_checkpoint_for_next.

title: stage09_llm_filter resumes by integer index into a file that upstream regenerates each run
summary: progress.json stores last_processed index; resume slices shortlisted_jobs.json from index+1. stage09_local_filter rewrites that file (content and order change) every run, so a resume after re-shortlisting analyzes wrong jobs and skips others.
impact: Wrong or missing Gemini analyses after any interrupted run followed by a re-shortlist.
what_could_go_wrong: Key exhaustion at job 40/100 on Monday; Tuesday's run regenerates the shortlist (different order), resumes at index 41 of the new list — 40 arbitrary jobs skipped unanalyzed.
recommendation: Resume by job_id against its own SQLite table (UNIQUE(job_id) already exists); delete progress.json (Roadmap 2.6).
alternatives: Include a shortlist-file hash in progress.json and invalidate on mismatch (band-aid).
evidence: start_index = progress['last_processed'] + 1 with no consistency check against file identity.

title: genai.configure global-state race in threaded run_batch — requests can use and account the wrong API key
summary: genai.configure(api_key=...) mutates process-global SDK state; run_batch executes _process_single_request in up to 16 threads. Thread B's configure can land between thread A's configure and generate_content.
impact: Key attribution, quota counting, and cooldown state become wrong under parallelism; a single key can absorb all traffic and 429.
what_could_go_wrong: CLI --batch with speed=max: both keys' token buckets show healthy while one key actually serves everything and gets rate-limited.
recommendation: Lock around configure+call, or migrate to google-genai Client instances (key per client object) (Roadmap 2.4). Latent today: production path is sequential.
alternatives: One worker per key with per-worker configure.
evidence: configure at 507 inside worker function; ThreadPoolExecutor submit loop at 689-693; max_workers default min(len(keys)*2,16).

title: Homemade Gemini rate-limit engine (token bucket + daily quota + cooldowns) persisted to dot-files, with double sleep in the call path
summary: BURST/RATE_PER_MIN/20-per-day constants hardcode free-tier assumptions; usage state is written to data/.key_usage.json inside the lock on every request; a mandatory sleep(1.2) in the client is duplicated by another sleep(1.2) in the caller.
impact: ~2.4s of pure sleep per analyzed job; quota logic is bespoke code to maintain; tier changes require code edits.
what_could_go_wrong: Upgrading to a paid tier: the code still throttles to 20/day/key until someone finds the constant.
recommendation: Single sleep owned by the client; constants to config; consider tenacity + a 30-line quota tracker (Roadmap 2.4).
alternatives: google-genai SDK retry/backoff options.
evidence: sleep at gemini_client:523 and stage09_llm_filter:506 both execute per job in the production path.

title: Entire nightly run is synchronous and serialized end to end
summary: GPU OCR → per-line translation → sequential Ollama batches → sleep-gated sequential Gemini → 1.5s-spaced Telegram. Appropriate for a nightly batch, but avoidable fixed costs exist (per-line Argos calls, doubled Gemini sleeps, downloader worker pool of 1).
impact: Longer nightly window than necessary; a slow stage pushes completion toward the next morning's download with no overlap protection (F-005).
what_could_go_wrong: A 30-page Hindi-heavy day makes translation+OCR overrun into the 11:50 downloader.
recommendation: Targeted fixes only (batch Argos per file, restore downloader workers, concurrent 2-key Gemini). Do NOT rewrite to asyncio.
alternatives: Ollama num_parallel=2 after VRAM check (hypothesis to verify).
evidence: smart_translate_block called per line; workers=1 comment 'Reduced to 1 for debugging'.

title: SQLite sprawl: 4 live single-table DBs + 1 orphan, inline DDL at call sites, no migrations, mixed timestamp formats
summary: Schema exists only as CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS strings scattered across four files (one executed per logged request); no version tracking; naive-local, UTC+Z, and raw-datetime timestamps coexist; deprecated sqlite3 datetime adapter used on Python 3.12.
impact: Schema evolution requires manual surgery per DB file; cross-DB queries impossible; time comparisons unreliable across tables.
what_could_go_wrong: Adding attempts tracking to sent_jobs: ALTER TABLE by hand on production or silent divergence; positional readers (F-025) misread.
recommendation: core/storage.py + one scanner.db + user_version migration ladder (Roadmap 2.1); delete/archive progress.db.
alternatives: SQLAlchemy Core + Alembic later if warranted.
evidence: Query-site inventory in sqlite-query-surface.csv (23 sites); datetime.now() bound directly at stage07:681.

title: Duplicated SQL access code and positional tuple coupling across stages
summary: get_new_jobs/get_all_jobs are copy-paste twins; sent_jobs rows are unpacked positionally in stage10 (job[5]); init_db boilerplate exists three times.
impact: Any column addition/reorder silently corrupts the notifier's field mapping.
what_could_go_wrong: Adding a 'city' column between similarity and match_score shifts every downstream index by one — messages show scores in the similarity slot.
recommendation: Typed row accessors in core/storage.py (Roadmap 2.1).
alternatives: sqlite3.Row + name-based access as a minimal patch.
evidence: Cited lines; SELECT column lists differ from consumer expectations only by convention.

title: All 12 web sources depend on one unofficial aggregator (epaperwave.com); fallback is one unofficial Telegram channel
summary: A single third-party site redistributing newspaper PDFs (via Google Drive) is the sole web ingestion path; one Telegram channel is the only fallback. Both are unlicensed redistributors that can vanish or change without notice.
impact: Single point of failure for 100% of ingestion; latent legal/ToS exposure; anti-bot escalation risk concentrated on one target.
what_could_go_wrong: Takedown or redesign of epaperwave → zero papers until a new source strategy is built under time pressure.
recommendation: Diversify: Telegram-first, evaluate official e-paper/RSS/government job-portal sources for partial coverage (Roadmap 3.2).
alternatives: Licensed e-paper subscriptions for the 3-4 highest-value papers.
evidence: All web_sources URLs share the epaperwave.com domain; downloader phase 3 targets channel_id -1002797473616.

title: 2,821-line downloader: deep heuristic cascade, three GDrive implementations, stale anti-bot fingerprint, and shipped debug configuration
location: src/downloader/newspaper_downloader.py:657-707 (20 date formats), 833-1592 (cascading preprocessors), 1709/2086 (duplicate GDrive), 2806 (workers=1 'for debugging'); configs/newspaper_config.json (headless:false, Chrome-91 UA)
summary: Edition discovery layers date-regexes, fuzzy name matching (0.65), attribute/JS mining, iframe scans, and HEAD probes with no telemetry about which layer matched; Google Drive handling exists three times; production runs one worker headful with a 2021 user agent.
impact: Every source breakage adds another layer; wrong-edition downloads pass validation; scheduled runs require a display; degradation is invisible until yield hits zero.
what_could_go_wrong: Fuzzy match pulls 'IE Chandigarh' instead of 'IE Delhi' for weeks — valid PDFs, wrong city, nobody notices.
recommendation: Hardening pass: one GDrive impl, per-layer match telemetry, yield alarm, headless:true, workers=3 (Roadmap 0.3/2.9); strategic source shift per F-026.
alternatives: Playwright port for the residual scraping after the cascade is slimmed (Roadmap 3.2).
evidence: Function map and line ranges from full read; config values from redacted config dump.

title: Downloader failures are invisible: exit status discarded by scheduler, detection is log-lines only, and its debug artifacts are deleted nightly
summary: main() returns success if ≥1 file downloaded (1 of 14 is 'success'); the scheduler ignores even that; per-source failures live only in newspaper_downloader.log; debug HTML dumps land under raw_pdfs/debug and are wiped by stage11.
impact: Partial and total ingestion failures produce no signal, and the evidence to diagnose them is destroyed the same night.
what_could_go_wrong: 10 of 14 sources quietly failing for a month while the 4 survivors keep the exit code green.
recommendation: Expected-vs-actual source-count Telegram report (Roadmap 1.2/2.9); persist debug dumps outside the cleaned tree with a TTL.
alternatives: Orchestrator sensor on downloaded-file count.
evidence: return total_downloaded > 0; scheduler backgrounds with '|| echo Command exited non-zero' into the log.

title: Secrets hygiene: git-clean but disk-loose (live keys, bot token file, Telethon session at repo root)
location: .gitignore; configs/gemini_config.json (real keys on disk); token_telegram/Jobs_sidd_bot.txt; telegram_session_newspaper_wave_10.session (repo root); .env
summary: All secret files are correctly gitignored (verified against git ls-files), but real API keys, a bot token, and an authenticated Telethon session sit in plaintext inside the working tree, including at the repo root.
impact: Any directory share, backup, or accidental 'git add -f' exposes credentials; the session file grants full account access to the Telegram user.
what_could_go_wrong: Zipping the project directory to share for debugging ships the Telegram session and Gemini keys.
recommendation: Move session/token files out of the repo tree (e.g., ~/.config/smart-job-scanner/); keep configs example-only with env interpolation.
alternatives: git-crypt/age for at-rest encryption if they must stay in-tree.
evidence: git ls-files shows only example configs tracked; ls shows the listed files present on disk.

title: Nine-plus fragmented state mechanisms with no unified run identity
location: run_state/*.done; data/progress/*.json; cache_blocks/; processing_state.db+checkpoint; llm_results/progress.json; shortlist_history.db; telegram watermark; .download_state.json; .key_usage.json/.key_validation_cache.json
summary: Each stage invented its own persistence (markers, JSON dicts, checkpoints, watermarks, skip lists, quota files). No run ID ties any of them together; semantics differ per mechanism.
impact: Resume correctness varies wildly per stage (F-014/F-019/F-020); no query can answer 'what happened to run X'; every new feature adds a tenth mechanism.
what_could_go_wrong: Partial-failure recovery requires editing three unrelated state stores in the right order — undocumented tribal knowledge.
recommendation: Run-state DB + boundary manifests (Roadmap 2.2); orchestrator state ownership longer term.
alternatives: Dagster asset materializations model this natively.
evidence: Inventory in 01-system-inventory.md §6 with per-mechanism citations.

title: File-based IPC without manifests: downstream cannot distinguish 'upstream empty' from 'upstream failed'
location: All stage boundaries (see pipeline-stage-matrix.csv); metadata re-parsed from filenames via _p(\d+) regexes in stages 02/04/06
summary: Stage contracts are directory globs and filename regexes; no counts, schemas, or run identity cross boundaries. Page/paper identity round-trips through filename string operations.
impact: Silent no-op propagation (with F-002); newspaper names containing '_p' or format drift corrupt page attribution.
what_could_go_wrong: A paper named 'Deccan_perald' (OCR-mangled folder) splits wrongly at '_p', attributing all pages to page 'erald'.
recommendation: _manifest.json per boundary dir (count, run_id, produced_at); consumers verify (Roadmap 2.2).
alternatives: Dagster assets; or SQLite-backed artifact registry.
evidence: extract_prefix splits on '_p' (stage06:33-35); stage04 page regex at 296-299,1317-1322.

title: No packaging; CWD-dependent relative paths; module-level side effects make stages untestable and unrelocatable
location: No pyproject.toml; sys.path hacks (stage02:20, stage09_llm_filter:24); Path('data/...') throughout; import-time effects: stage03:31 (tesseract warm-up), stage04:126-136 (CUDA env), stage09_dynamic_resumes:70 (GitHub auth), stage10:38-41 (SystemExit on missing env)
summary: Stages execute as file paths from a fixed CWD; importing them triggers network auth, OCR warm-up, environment mutation, or process exit.
impact: Unit testing requires the elaborate placeholder-env fixture that exists in tests/test_imports.py; nothing can run from another directory or machine.
what_could_go_wrong: Any tool that imports a stage module (linter plugin, REPL, future test) authenticates to GitHub or exits the process.
recommendation: pyproject.toml, python -m execution, core/paths.py with SCANNER_HOME, push side effects behind main() (Roadmap 2.8/3.3).
alternatives: None better; this is standard packaging hygiene.
evidence: Cited import-time code; tests/test_imports.py:41-56 fixture exists solely to survive imports.

title: Dead scaffolding: four utility modules with zero importers, unused composite runner, orphaned DB, stale docs
location: src/utils/state_manager.py, logging_utils.py, file_utils.py; src/llm/llm_utils.py; src/pipeline/stage09_resume_matching.py; progress.db; src/README.md (documents pre-refactor scripts as production)
summary: grep confirms no imports of the four utility modules; the composite stage-09 runner is unreferenced; progress.db has no code references; src/README.md contradicts run_pipeline.sh about what production executes.
impact: Readers (and future refactors) waste time on code that does nothing; docs actively mislead.
what_could_go_wrong: Someone 'fixes' logging by editing logging_utils.py and nothing changes.
recommendation: Delete all of it; rewrite src/README.md to match reality (Roadmap 1.6).
alternatives: Adopt the utils layer for real (more work, same outcome available via core/ refactor).
evidence: grep -rn imports across src/scripts/tests: zero hits for the four modules; pipeline_config.json stage list excludes stage09_resume_matching.

title: Log sprawl: 888 files, per-stage ad-hoc logging config, cleanup misses non-.log artifacts, repo root littered
location: logs/ (888 files incl. failed_batches/, raw_responses/, tuning*/); stage11_cleanup.py:168-186 (only *.log pruned); ~30 loose logs/PNGs/.deb at repo root; gemini_interactions_log.json tracked in git

title: cache_blocks/ preprocessing cache is unbounded and effectively write-only (629 MB and growing)
summary: Cache keys are blake2b hashes of absolute source paths; source folders are date-named so entries never hit again after their day; nothing evicts (stage11 cleans only data/; --no-cache clears but is never passed).
impact: Pure disk leak: ~tens of MB per paper per day retained forever with near-zero hit rate after day one.
what_could_go_wrong: Disk exhaustion on the GPU box; OCR then fails in confusing ways (no free-space checks).
recommendation: Age-based eviction at stage start (delete entries older than 2 days) or key the cache under data/ so stage11 handles it.
alternatives: Drop the cache: measure first — pages are read once per run, the cache may not pay for itself at all.
evidence: du -sh cache_blocks = 629M; _cache_for_path hashes str(img_path); daily folder names include dates.

title: No internal health interface, admin surface, or failure alerting; health_check.py is manual preflight only

recommendation: Telegram failure hook + nightly digest (Roadmap 1.2); scanner status/retry CLI (2.3); Prefect UI as the eventual dashboard (3.1). A custom web dashboard is explicitly not recommended.

title: Scheduler bash mechanics are one refactor away from boot failure; catch-up times duplicated from jobs.conf
location: scripts/scheduler.sh:29-40 ((i++)) under set -e saved only by '|| true'), 54-57 (unguarded compute_next), 111-113 (hardcoded 11:50/23:30)
summary: set -eo pipefail interacts fragilely with arithmetic post-increment and unguarded function calls; the startup catch-up logic hardcodes job times that also live in jobs.conf.
impact: A malformed jobs.conf time or an innocent refactor (removing '|| true') kills the daemon at boot; changing a schedule in one place silently diverges from the other.
what_could_go_wrong: Job time edited to '11:50 AM' → date -d fails → compute_next returns 1 → set -e exits during boot loop → no scheduling at all.
recommendation: Retired wholesale by systemd timers (Roadmap 0.2) — do not patch bash.
alternatives: If keeping bash: set -u, guard all calls, single source of schedule truth.
evidence: Cited lines; behavior reasoning verified against bash semantics of compound commands with || true.

title: MAX_RETRIES=0 means intentional infinite retry; the Python runner variant retries with zero delay
summary: Bash documents 0 as unlimited (backoff caps at 300s, loops forever, no alert); the Python port loops with no sleep at all.
impact: A permanently-failing stage spins the night away (bash) or hot-loops the CPU (python).
what_could_go_wrong: Env var MAX_RETRIES=0 set during debugging and forgotten; next real failure never terminates.
recommendation: Remove the unlimited mode; cap total retry wall-time; alert on exhaustion (subsumed by Roadmap 1.1/1.2).
alternatives: Orchestrator retry policies.
evidence: Cited lines; python loop lacks any time.sleep in the failure branch.

title: stage03 refiner discards blocks silently with debug sampling disabled (rate 0.0) and swallows exceptions into counters
summary: Filtering decisions (tiny/graphic/short-text) permanently drop content with no retained sample for QA; worker exceptions become a 'skipped_error' count with no traceback persisted.

what_could_go_wrong: A threshold tweak drops 20% of legitimate ads; nothing surfaces it.
recommendation: Sample 1-2% of skipped blocks to a QA dir with a retention window; log tracebacks for skipped_error.

title: stage08 dedup is O(n²) SequenceMatcher over all job lines per issue

title: .done markers keyed to full command string, no run/date scoping; manual runs after success silently no-op
